• | Thus far in the fourth quarter of 2026, 68% of the available VLCC spot days have been booked at an average rate of $579,900 per day on a discharge-to-discharge basis. 86% of the available VLCC days, combined spot and time charter days, have been booked at an average rate of $267,500 per day.

desk.headline: Revenue roughly tripled to $332.4m and profit hit $270.9m; Q4 spot days 68% booked at $579,900 a day

other.label: Ordinary EPS (excl. vessel sale gain and derivatives)

results: Revenue roughly tripled to $332.4m as spot VLCCs earned $167,100 a day, up from $38,700 a year ago.
Profit was $270.9m ($1.68 a share), including a $34.2m gain on selling DHT Bauhinia.
Excluding that gain and a derivatives gain, ordinary profit was $234.5m, or $1.45 a share, above the $1.26 consensus.
The full $1.45 of ordinary earnings is paid as a dividend, the 67th quarterly payout in a row.
Two VLCCs were fixed on 3-year charters at $75,000 and $100,000 a day; a new VLCC was ordered for April 2029 delivery.

guidance.summary: DHT gives no profit forecast, but says 68% of Q4 spot days are booked at $579,900 a day and 86% of all Q4 days at $267,500 a day.

watch: How the remaining 32% of Q4 spot days are fixed, given very high booked rates so far.
Shipping disruption and Strait of Hormuz risk, which the company says keep the freight market tight.
Dividend size, which moves with ordinary earnings, and spending on the newly ordered VLCC.
